title: Adaptive request pacing with queued deprioritization for Dedicated fleets
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Implement a per-customer adaptive request pacing system that combines token-bucket admission with a short prioritized queue and automated deprioritization heuristics. Goal is to provide predictable throughput and latency SLOs for Dedicated fleets while reducing wasted GPU work during transient overloads.

Why: Current Dedicated ingress either accepts or rejects beyond static caps, causing spikes of latency or hard rejects under temporary bursts. We need a more graceful mechanism that preserves priority for high-value traffic, sheds low-value requests early, and cooperates with autoscaler signals to avoid oscillations and wasted scaling events.

Scope: Design and implement runtime changes to admission path, control-plane policies to configure per-customer pacing parameters, and Console controls/visibility. Include telemetry, safety knobs, and a canary rollout for fleets in staging and a subset of customers in production.
acceptance_criteria: Configurable per-customer token-bucket rate and burst parameters exposed in Dedicated config
Short-lived FIFO per-priority queue (max latency window default 250ms) that allows higher priority requests to preempt lower priority requests in the queue
Deprioritization rules: automated tag-based deprioritization (e.g., background embeddings, low-tier keys) that move requests to best-effort queue or drop after timeout
Integration with autoscaler: pacing should reduce admission rate to prevent unnecessary scale-ups and surface a metric used by autoscaler to make scaling decisions
End-to-end tests validating SLO preservation under 2x and 5x burst conditions and unit tests for priority logic
Dashboard panels showing admitted vs dropped vs queued rates, queue latency distribution, and per-customer pacing parameters
Canary rollout plan executed and validated with rollback criteria (CPU/GPU utilization, 95th latency, and error rate thresholds)
technical_design: Admission path: add a per-customer token-bucket check at ingress with configurable refill and burst. Tokens consumed on request start; requests without tokens may enter short priority queue or be shed immediately according to policy.

Queueing: implement an in-memory, bounded queue per fleet with priority lanes (high, normal, best-effort). Queue capacity expressed as token-equivalent or request-count. Queue eviction uses oldest-first within same priority; lower-priority entries are evicted first when global headroom low.

Deprioritization: rules engine evaluates request metadata (api_key_tier, endpoint, client_tags) and assigns priority. A background job will periodically convert queued normal requests to best-effort when headroom < threshold.

Autoscaler feedback: expose a new metric 'admission_pressure' derived from token-bucket deficit and queue fill percentage. Autoscaler will consume this metric to avoid scaling for transient bursts below configured scale threshold.

Fallbacks: when queue exceeds absolute cap or a request hits max-queue-delay, system will trigger graceful fallback (route to cheaper model variant or return structured rate-limited response indicating recommended retry-after).
Circuit-breaking: incorporate per-fleet emergency-open circuit that forces immediate shedding if cluster enters overload state (GPU OOM risk or sustained 95th-latency > X).
Config storage: per-customer policies stored in control-plane store with quick update propagation to node agents using optimistic caches and versioned policies.
Backward compatibility: existing static caps still accepted; this system augments rather than replaces them. Default policies mirror prior behavior for customers not opted in.
monitoring_and_alerting: Metrics: dedicated.admissions.admitted, dedicated.admissions.queued, dedicated.admissions.dropped, dedicated.queue.latency.p95, dedicated.token_deficit_per_customer
Dashboards: per-fleet panel with stacked admitted/queued/dropped timeseries and histogram of queue latency; per-customer heatmap of token-deficit over 24h
Alerts: P1 alert when dropped_rate > 1% sustained for 10m for production fleets; P0 alert when queue_latency.p95 > 500ms or admission_pressure > 0.8 for 5m
SLO check: continuous evaluation that 99% of priority=high requests have latency < SLO under 2x baseline load.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev/staging): unit + integration tests, run on staging Dedicated clusters with synthetic bursts (2x, 5x). Duration: 2 weeks.
Phase 1 (canary-prod small fleet): enable for non-critical customer subset (10% of Dedicated fleets) with verbose telemetry. Duration: 1 week validation window.
Phase 2 (opt-in customers): gradually opt other customers with informed consent and provide console toggles. Duration: rolling over 3 weeks.
Phase 3 (default): enable defaults for all fleets; provide deprecation path and documentation. Duration: 2 weeks; monitor for regressions and rollback if thresholds exceeded.
Rollback criteria: sustained increase in 95th latency by >20% vs baseline, error rate increase >0.5% absolute, or spike in autoscaler churn exceeding historical variance.
test_plan: Unit tests for token-bucket math and priority assignment rules
Integration tests simulating mixed priority traffic with bursty patterns and asserting queue behavior
Chaos test: node eviction while queue draining to ensure no double-charge and safe shedding
Performance test: validate CPU/GPU overhead of queue/admission logic at production request rates (target <2% request-path CPU overhead)
End-to-end verification with sample deduped workloads and metric-based assertions in CI pipelines
